nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a real vector space with a topology and let $f : E \to [-\infty, \infty]$ never take the value $-\infty$. Then $f^{**}(x) \le f(x)$ for every $x \in E$, where $f^{**}$ is the Fenchel biconjugate of $f$.
nodes.title: The biconjugate lies below the function

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a real vector space with a topology and let $f : E \to [-\infty, \infty]$. The biconjugate of $f$ at $x \in E$ is the extended real number $f^{**}(x) = \sup_L \big(L(x) - f^*(L)\big)$, where $L$ ranges over the continuous linear functionals $E \to \mathbb{R}$ and $f^*$ is the Fenchel conjugate of $f$.
nodes.title: Fenchel biconjugate

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a real vector space with a topology and let $f : E \to [-\infty, \infty]$. The Fenchel conjugate of $f$ at a continuous linear functional $L : E \to \mathbb{R}$ is the extended real number $f^*(L) = \sup_{y \in E} \big(L(y) - f(y)\big)$.
nodes.title: Fenchel conjugate

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a locally convex real topological vector space, not necessarily Hausdorff. Let $f : E \to [-\infty, \infty]$ be lower semicontinuous, never equal to $-\infty$, not identically $+\infty$, and convex in the sense that the set $\{(x, r) \in E \times \mathbb{R} : f(x) \le r\}$ is convex. nodes.title: Fenchel–Moreau theorem

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a topological space and let $f : E \to [-\infty, \infty]$ be lower semicontinuous. Then the set $\{(x, r) \in E \times \mathbb{R} : f(x) \le r\}$ is closed in $E \times \mathbb{R}$.
nodes.title: Lower semicontinuous functions have closed epigraphs
